messages:
sahil: Quick heads-up — noticed a weird drop in cache hit-rate on RAG workloads after last kernel swap :confused:
maya: details?
sahil: On the canary (r12->r13 kernels) we're seeing prefix cache hit-rate drop from ~82% -> ~62% for our docs-level RAG tests. p50 latency up ~12% on completions.
ian: do we have a small repro we can run locally?
sahil: yes, I ran a 100k synthetic request sweep. Two traffic patterns: (A) chat-style convo priming, (B) direct completion prompts used by customers for RAG. Chat priming hit-rate stayed ~79-82%, completions collapsed to ~58-63 depending on tokenizer.
jessica: what's the cache key pipeline today?
sahil: we construct a key by concatenating [user_prefix, system_meta_json, conversation_context] (as strings), then murmur3_64 over the bytes. No further normalization.
maya: any signs of tokenization shifts? r13 pulled in the fused tokenization path last week.
ian: exactly — r13's tokenizer produces different piece boundaries for punctuation and some unicode sequences, so raw-string keys can diverge even when semantics are identical.
sahil: short log excerpt from failing pair: 
```
# same logical prompt, two keys
prompt_A -> key: 0x7fa1b3c
prompt_A_variant -> key: 0x9cde10f
diff bytes -> ", " vs ",\u00A0"  (nbspace)
```
jessica: oh nice catch — client copy/paste introduced non-breaking spaces and some metadata ordering differs (kv field order).
maya: that would fragment keys a lot for completions where templates are glued together on the client. Chat less affected because convo prefixes are repeated verbatim.
sahil: I ran a small normalization experiment on canary: whitespace & unicode normalize + sort JSON keys before hashing. Results: r12 baseline 83.1% -> r13 raw 61.9% -> r13 normalized 82.4% (workload A). Chat workload changed much less (78.9% -> 76.8% -> 78.6%).
perf-bot: quick sim summary (normalized): workload A (RAG short) — r12 83.1%, r13 raw 61.9%, r13 norm 82.4%. workload B (chat long) — r12 78.9%, r13 raw 76.8%, r13 norm 78.6%. Collision rate: r13 raw 0.01% -> r13 norm 0.02%.
jessica: two concerns: 1) coupling to tokenizer if we fingerprint post-tokenize; 2) making keys too permissive could raise collision risk.
ian: proposals: a) normalize unicode (NFKC), collapse whitespace, minify & sort metadata JSON before string-hash; b) optionally include a token-id fingerprint computed with the canonical tokenizer (stable interface) — tradeoffs noted. Also consider moving from 64-bit to 128-bit hash to keep collision chance negligible if normalization reduces entropy.
sahil: action plan I propose:
- Implement string-level normalization (unicode NFKC, collapse whitespace, strip trailing invisibles) in cache key gen (sahil)
- Canonicalize metadata JSON by sorting keys + minify before joining (jessica)
- Add an opt-in flag to generate token-id fingerprint keys for customers who opt into tokenizer-coupled keys (engineering discussion) (ian)
- Temporarily enable normalization flag on canary routing for the r13 lane (maya)
- Monitor collision rate & hit-rate for 72h, revert quickly if bad regressions.
maya: assign & ETA?
sahil: I'll push a small patch for normalization + tests today; canary by tomorrow morning.
jessica: I'll write the JSON canonicalizer in the next 8 hours and add unit tests for order invariance.
ian: I'll scope the token-id fingerprint design doc and estimate risk for kernel swaps. Recommend 128-bit hashing if we normalize to avoid edge collisions.
perf-bot: ran a quick collision scan on normalization build: collisions 0.02% (unchanged materially). Also measured p50 — normalization add negligible CPU in key path (~0.1ms).
sahil: perfect. will post canary metrics once we have 24h of data.
maya: added to eng-runtime board and pinged infra to observe any side-effects on batching heuristics (if keys change, batching grouping might shift). cc @ian
ian: good call — batching/cardinality interplay is important: if keys group differently we might see smaller batch sizes on hot paths; will keep an eye.
sahil: TL;DR: regression looked like kernel/tokenizer boundary changing raw-string keys, normalization fixes hit-rate for RAG completions; follow-up: evaluate token-id fingerprint and consider bigger hash size.
maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
